subject: HearthWave Dedicated Fleet: sizing plan, safety buffer, and onboarding steps
messages:
From: Anne Park <anne@hearthwave.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated fleet sizing request — Q3 model launch

Hi Lukas,

Quick context: HearthWave is launching a new multimodal assistant (small ensemble of 3 models) in early Q3. We want dedicated capacity to guarantee latency and predictable unit cost. We ran a short pilot on shared endpoints and are attaching our Q2 utilization export so you can see tail/median token throughput.

Can your team recommend a sizing approach (committed GPUs vs burst pool) and a phased onboarding? Key constraints:
- 95th pct latency target: 250ms for text-gen p95 (offloading embeddings to shared)
- expected sustained concurrency: ~110 simultaneous sessions, average 120 tokens/sec per session during peak windows
- retention/observability: we need 90d trace retention for first 30d of launch, then 30d thereafter

Attachment: hwu_usage_q2.csv (exported from our monitoring)

Would appreciate a short mutual action plan + rough cost delta for a baseline committed configuration vs a hybrid commit+burst.

Thanks,
Anne Park
Head of Infrastructure | HearthWave
anne@hearthwave.ai
+1 415-555-0134

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet sizing request — Q3 model launch

Thanks Anne — got the export and skimmed the 95/99 profiles. Looping Ben (sales lead, committed sizing) and Laura (solutions / capacity planning).

Initial thoughts (high level):
- The traffic profile looks bursty with long tails; a pure committed floor plus small burst pool is likely the most cost-predictable approach.
- We should instrument a short (2‑week) trial where we:
  1) mirror production traffic into a dedicated staging pool to validate latency at p95/p99,
  2) run a KV-prefix cache for warm sessions to lower token compute, and
  3) capture realistic sequence lengths for kernel selection.

Action items I propose:
- Ben: provide back-of-envelope pricing for 8 H100-equivalent GPUs committed vs 12 committed + 8 burst credits.
- Laura: run a quick capacity simulation (using their CSV) to map concurrency->gpu-hrs and identify where autoscale steps should trigger.
- Anne: confirm the launch date window and whether any regulatory constraints require VPC/private deployment.

We can put together a one-page mutual action plan and an SOW draft once we align on the commit shape.

Best,
Lukas Meyer

Thanks Luka s — confirming launch target: first beta release 2026-08-15, GA 2026-09-20. No special VPC constraints for beta; GA will require VPC + customer-managed KMS.

We attached the CSV with 1-min resolution for April–May and a small sample of traces for long sessions. A few notes:
- Peak 1-min concurrent sessions hit 128 on May 18 (spike from ad promo). Typical daily peaks: 80–110.
- Token distribution: median 45 tokens per request, 95th 420 tokens.
- We expect a steady growth of ~20% month-over-month after GA for at least 3 months.

Attachments: hwu_usage_q2.csv

Prefer a staged commit: baseline commit to cover 95th day-to-day without burst, with burst credits for marketing-driven spikes. Can you show the incremental cost delta versus our current shared spend?

Anne

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anne Park <anne@hearthwave.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed sizing + SOW stub (HWU-4821)

Anne / Lukas — pulled a quick sizing using the CSV and our utilization model. Notes and recommendation below.

Recommendation (baseline -> phased):
1) Baseline commit: 10 H100-equivalent GPUs dedicated (covers steady peaks ~110 concurrent with caching improvements).
2) Phase 1 (GA): add 6 burst-enabled GPUs (on-demand convertible credits) to handle marketing spikes and growth runway.
3) Safety buffer: +10% headroom on GPU-hours for first 90 days to protect p95 SLA during kernel tuning and warmup.

Why this shape:
- 10 committed GPUs gives predictable unit costs and handles the 95th day-to-day based on current sequences and our kernel mix assumptions.
- Burst pool lets you absorb 25–30% sudden concurrency increases without long lead provisioning.
- Safety buffer reduces risk for the first 30–90 days while we calibrate caching and batchers.

Estimated delta vs current shared spend (very rough):
- Your current average monthly shared spend: ~$85k/month.
- Proposed committed + burst blended: ~$155k/month (first quarter includes safety buffer and onboarding costs).
- We can provide a 10% credit on commit for Q3 to lower transition friction.

Attachments: hw-4821-draft-sow.pdf (SOW outlines onboarding, measurement windows, observability retention options)

Next steps I propose:
- Anne: confirm you want us to model a 10 vs 12 vs 14 committed scenario for sensitivity.
- Lukas: I’ll need the mutual action plan template and legal contact to start SOW routing if they want to proceed.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed sizing + SOW stub (HWU-4821)

Quick internal note — agree with Ben's sizing approach. A couple of operational asks before we finalize SOW:
- Observability: set default 90d token-level traces for the first 30d then roll to 30d (Anne requested this). Add an opt-in for extended retention as a billable add-on.
- Autoscale policy: suggest two-step autoscale (10% and 30% spike thresholds) with warm standbys to avoid cold-start latency.
- Discounting: confirm whether 10% introductory credit should be applied to committed fees only or to total blended monthly for Q3.

If we include those operational guarantees in the SOW and call out the measurement windows (two-week staging window + 30d calibration), we reduce SLA risk and should get a smoother onboarding.

I'll sync with Solutions Eng to add an observability appendix and draft the autoscale gating.

Laura Bennett
